neighbours.label: unclear: a preposition or verb that opens the complement of the preceding predicate (coated with, letter from, confident because of)
fire: Make sure every slice of chicken is coated with the spice mixture.
She was thrilled to receive a letter from her old teacher.
We booked our flight to Rome with a small regional airline.
They were hopeful because of the progress made last year.
The painting reminds visitors of the value of quiet moments in the garden.
He refused to accept the offer without seeing the contract.
The children were covered with mud after the football match.
I got a postcard from my sister while she was in Peru.
quiet: Make sure every slice of chicken is placed on the hot grill.
She was thrilled to see her old teacher at the station.
We booked our flight to Rome last Tuesday evening.
They were hopeful and the progress made last year was real.
The painting shows visitors a quiet moment in the garden.
He refused the offer and walked out of the room.
The children were tired and muddy after the football match.
I got a postcard yesterday while my sister was in Peru.

notes: No single token dominates; prepositions ' of', ' to', ' with', ' from'. Expected to fail.
